title: epipactis palustris f. ericetorum
intro: Epipactis palustris f. ericetorum, commonly known as marsh helleborine, is a rare and lesser-known variant of the epipactis palustris species, belonging to the orchid family. The marsh helleborine has been traditionally used in folk medicine, offering several health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antifungal properties, which can aid in treating various ailments such as respiratory issues and wounds. The therapeutic actions of Epipactis palustris f. ericetorum include its ability to relax muscles, reduce spasms, and exhibit sedative effects. Its bioactive constituents include iridoid glycosides, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
